notes.title: DEVLOG #6 - Boss Teasing & Advanced Game Modes
notes.content:
Hello again, and welcome to the [b]final devlog before [i]Drop Duchy[/i]’s release[/b]! I hope you’re ready to play this tiny game I started in my bedroom two years ago. 

Do you want a final dose of insight into what you can expect from the game? Well, you’re in luck because today I’m revealing (for the first time!) the [b]two other bosses[/b] and the [b]challenging modes[/b] for the courageous who can complete a run.

[h3]The Wall, The Keep, The Dungeon[/h3]
I didn’t think about adding bosses to [i]Drop Duchy[/i] until it was pretty advanced – but as soon as I realized that it could be an awesome addition to the game, I had this intention: each boss should be a [b]scary[/b] and [b]challenging[/b] mega-structure.

You’ve already discovered and faced [b]The Wall[/b] in the demo, a boss whose design evolved throughout development to ensure it was achievable using all sorts of strategies. The Wall is [b]mobile[/b], forcing you to play compactly and place pieces (including additional enemies) in sub-optimal positions. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/5d0fac547990c110e108841dbb55cf6556fd90d0.jpg[/img]
At the end of Act 2, you’ll face [b]The Keep[/b], which has an entirely different design: strong, sturdy, and impassible. The Keep is already placed on a massive grid and has [b]many units[/b] to begin with. The additional challenge here is to [b]avoid boosting its surveillance towers[/b], which is easier said than done since they watch over most of the grid! The wide grid and abundance of terrains make some buildings easier to play, but on the other hand, large buildings are more challenging to place.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/1be483f87a20c34cd8cf03a83c0ca5e01d2533ed.gif[/img]

But The Keep is relatively simple compared to the game’s final boss, [b]The Dungeon[/b]. 
First, The Dungeon has "[b]traps[/b]" that grant [b]additional units for every piece placed over them[/b] (not just the buildings!), and their position changes every time. 
Second, it recruits additional Mercenaries every few turns unless you [b]bribe[/b] them first: yes, to beat the final boss, collecting resources through exploration & buildings is essential to prevent him from gaining too much power too quickly!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/d9ca5c3b20785aed3776e7df79661874107a72d8.gif[/img]

The bosses in [i]Drop Duchy[/i] have been tested a lot, and we ensured that all sorts of strategies are viable against them. Yes, they’re hard, but that’s the point of bosses, right?

[h3]Raise the Difficulty[/h3]
When you’ve defeated [i]The Dungeon[/i], you win the run! Does the game end there? "Pack it up, boys, we’re uninstalling it to make some room on the SSD"? Of course not! 
First, you can try to [b]complete every quest[/b] and [b]challenge[/b] to finish the progress tree, and second, you can play again with a greater challenge.

There are [b]two modes in the game[/b]: [b][u]Classic[/u][/b] & [b][u]Trials[/u][/b]. 

[b]Classic[/b] comes in [b]five difficulties[/b], so if you want to challenge your strategic skills, try beating the game with each faction up to [b]Nightmare mode[/b]. As difficulty increases, you’ll face [b]more enemy units[/b], receive [b]fewer resources[/b] from exploration, and you [b]won't be able to place the enemy pieces in reserve[/b] anymore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/fd5dfeb4080a7d1a3fbfa92a9508db56624eb67b.jpg[/img]
[b]Trials[/b], on the other hand, are [b]unlocked after beating the game for the first time[/b], and they’re variants that [b]alter the game’s rules[/b], making you think twice about the correct approach. 
Some Trials add fierce advantages to enemies; for instance, in [b]Consolidation mode[/b], placing two enemy buildings next to each other will grant both of them additional troops. 
Others, such as [b]Mini Grids[/b], will change which buildings are stronger or weaker (and make it generally more challenging to optimize the positioning). 
If you feel confident, you could even take on the [b]Fearless challenge[/b], in which you start the run with [b]a single point of defense[/b] and will therefore lose unless you eliminate all the enemies each round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/bdd195042087f61067714045a9bff04b055c5597.jpg[/img]
With such a variety of modes, we’re sure you’ll be able to spend countless hours in the game before getting bored (and I haven’t even talked about optimizing your high score). 
One last thing before the conclusion: we’ve added [b]seals[/b] to the cards in the [b]Collection menu[/b] to let you know the highest difficulty you’ve beaten the game with each card. As in Balatro (the game that inspired this mechanic), [b]you must use the card in the final encounter against The Dungeon to earn the seal[/b]. That’d be too easy if we let you gain the seal when you didn't use the card or if you sold it during the run – winning a Nightmare run with a Windmill is about as crazy as it sounds, but it is definitely doable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/26c337291324e351f235d549d5620a99b7cf0ac8.jpg[/img]
[h3]Wrap-Up[/h3]
Thanks for reading this last devlog of [i]Drop Duchy[/i]. I hope this series gave you a good sense of what you can expect in the game at its release. I also hope you’ll enjoy discovering and playing with all this content as much as I enjoyed working on it these past few years! 

Stay in touch by subscribing to the [url=https://sleepymillstudio.substack.com/]newsletter[/url] and joining the [url=https://discord.com/invite/Ekrchk7fHb]Discord server[/url].

notes.title: DEVLOG #5 - Faction The Order & Religious Cards
notes.content:
Hello!

[i]Drop Duchy[/i]’s release date is approaching, and I know all of you readers of these devlogs are on the edge of your seats, wondering what’s in the game beyond the demo you’ve had time to explore by now.
Well, today, I’m going to tell you all about the third faction of the game, The Order, but in order to understand it, we need to talk about a special family of cards: the religious buildings and the Faith mechanic.

[h3]Omnipotent Church[/h3]
Farming, cities, and artisans were essential to medieval life, and so is religion: leaving this crucial aspect out of the game would be like building a house without a roof! 
In our game, most religious cards award you [b]Faith[/b], a bonus stat that resets every round and boosts all the resources collected this round.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/c92d4d6d805f7541ce088621e9bd3ed21662ed59.gif[/img]

Religious buildings are, therefore, highly versatile and can fit every deck; boosting the resources from buildings and exploration can be a great accelerator to your economy. For instance, you can place a [b]Church[/b] anywhere in the grid to gain Faith instantly, get the technology card [b]Daily Bread[/b] to earn Faith when you explore Fields, or add the fantastic [b]Cathedral[/b] to your selection to double all Faith gains in its range!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/5e4c9f6536bf3b40821efc3c3e7fb2f67866e96a.gif[/img]

If you’re really into religious cards, you can specialize in them by including the other type of religious cards: those whose effect is multiplied by the number of Faith points you got in the round. This combo deck requires full commitment, but when you’ve got the right synergy, you’re unbeatable. For instance, the [b]Abbey[/b] earns as much as 20 Gold per Faith, the [b]Blessing[/b] tech can heal your Defense points, and there are even military buildings, such as the [b]Commandery[/b], which recruits 3 units per Faith!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/676b07a28d46b087320c9a8450165cd9665604d6.gif[/img]

[h3]Introducing: The Order[/h3]
Now that you know more about Faith and the religious cards, let me introduce the third and final faction of the game, [b]The Order[/b]. Since it’s the last you’ll unlock from the progress tree, we decided to step up the complexity, but if you handle it correctly, it’s at least as good, if not better, as the other two.

[b]The Order[/b] is a crusade-themed faction that relies on two core synergies: religious and military. Its starting building, [b]Krak des Chevaliers,[/b] is inspired by a real-life XII-century fortress built during the crusades. It’s a military building that is particularly tricky to place in the grid, but it can potentially recruit a considerable number of units, even in the first rounds of the run!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/52e9f804b7f20bc3094f9341c25bc684059cc5e8.gif[/img]

What’s the catch, you may ask? 

Unlike the other two factions, [b]The Order[/b] cannot spend gold to repair their defenses after a battle; they really need to win if they want to go far. On top of that, when the round ends, each remaining unit is turned into a [b]crusader[/b] rather than the usual gold, further increasing the challenge of getting a solid economy going. You can send the crusaders in [b]Expeditions[/b] in the dedicated menu to loot precious resources, strengthen your defense, or increase your baseline Faith.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/06faaf5a339f7a4df10a4c24a8c3df94a0251546.gif[/img]

With its more straightforward access to Faith, [b]The Order[/b] is the ideal faction to build a solid religious combo. After each round, you can use the earned Faith to improve the starting technology [b]Holy Crusade[/b], which influences how many resources you collect from Expeditions. If you need more crusaders, include the other faction-exclusive buildings of [b]The Order[/b], such as the [b]Military Chaplaincy[/b]. 
Playing with this faction feels easier at first because of its military advantage, but don’t forget about building a solid economy if you want to go far!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/f5f480e66a88be7ab91161aba6dbe012643a811e.gif[/img]

[h3]Wrap Up[/h3]
Thanks again for reading this devlog. We’re so excited to see you play with all the content we’ve crafted for you, and we hope you enjoy it like you enjoyed the demo! The next installment in this devlog series will also be the last before the game’s release, so we’ll touch on an all-important topic: [b]what are the other two bosses and the alternative game modes?[/b]
If you enjoy our game, please support us by joining the [url=https://discord.com/invite/Ekrchk7fHb]community on [b]Discord[/b][/url] and  [url=https://sleepymillstudio.substack.com/]subscribing to the studio newsletter[/url]. 

Thanks!

notes.title: DEVLOG #4 - Rivers & Mountains
notes.content:
Hello again! 

I’m back with another entry in the devlog series! 
Are you excited to learn more about [i]Drop Duchy[/i]? Well, you should be!

Since the last issue, we’ve launched the [b]updated demo[/b] that included the faction [b]Republic[/b] and a sneak peek at the [b]meta progression[/b]. With this demo, we entered the [b]Steam Next Fest[/b], a special event dedicated to showcasing upcoming games, and the response was fantastic. 
Thanks (and welcome) to everybody who discovered the game during the festival!

On the menu today, I’ll tell you more about a terrain you can unlock in the demo -[b]the River[/b]- but also answer the burning questions: [b]how long are the runs[/b], and what are the [b]other terrains[/b] available in the game?

[h3]Risking it all for the River[/h3]
When you start your journey, you’ll only see Plains & Forests, the two basic terrains of [i]Drop Duchy[/i]. Once you’re comfortable with the ropes of the game, you’ll be ready to start playing in the big league and unlock the [b]River terrain[/b] from the [b]Progress Tree[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/a8c450020b2122eb3698bba065ea8ea3763c6eb5.jpg[/img]

As you can expect, the river is at its best when it’s all [b]connected[/b] rather than being a bunch of isolated ponds, and that’s the reason why most river-related buildings have a mechanic called "[b]Minimum Flow[/b]," which requires [b]a large enough continuous river to activate their effect[/b]. Those effects are typically better than their forests/plains counterparts, but they’re harder to trigger if you don’t plan your grid strategically.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/b8cb69b9baf51afa12b91bb8f51d94f8d03d0cdc.gif[/img]

To help you assemble the longest connected river, you can rely on the [b]"Canal" technology card[/b] (which forces the river piece to come early in the round) or use the "[b]Bridge[/b]," which counts as a building and a chunk of river terrain! 
Going all in on the river and placing all your buildings correctly next to it is one of the most potent strategies in the game, albeit risky.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/bd9c649ae63c38aa0e80a1d2419d1837440bfa00.jpg[/img]

[h3]Mighty Mountains[/h3]
If you’ve played the demo, you’ve probably noticed that some buildings require stone to be upgraded to their maximum level, yet you couldn’t find any way to get some. It’s not a bug, but a feature: [b]stone is only introduced in the game’s second act[/b], with the addition of [b]Mountains[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/dd0746db6f4882d949153c0de39bab6367e6657a.jpg[/img]

Mountains differ from the previous terrains because all [b]their effects take into account the whole piece rather than individual squares[/b], and unlike the others, [b]there is no way to transform the mountains[/b]. As you can imagine, mountains earn you the precious stone resource when explored, but they also come with a flurry of buildings that synergize with them: the "[b]Stone Cutter[/b]" is ideal if you want to increase the stone yield, while the "[b]Fortress[/b]" is a fantastic military building that recruits troops for each aligned mountain piece.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/e1c2f8b0e8f87d9f84250f9d2764836292846bea.gif[/img]

Tweaking your deck to include a mountain synergy can be challenging, but remember that you can sell any card (and get the upgrade resources refunded), making pivoting strategy much easier. 
Mountain-related buildings tend to be better than the others, but since you can only start adding them to your deck in Act 2, you have fewer chances to grab them, and therefore, you must be an excellent strategist. 
Speaking of which, there’s one crucial choice you’ll have to make as you progress: [b]which terrains do you specialize in[/b]?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/aae70e7bb42f19f93d254e1d782e9f8bb50d376b.jpg[/img]

[h3]How Terrain Specialization Works?[/h3]
As you may have noticed in the demo, there are fewer pieces of each when there are more terrains on a grid (simple maths, really). That’s the normal intended way to play the game (trust me, there is little challenge in grids with a single terrain type), but it raises the question: [b]how do we introduce more terrains without breaking the game’s balance[/b]? Our solution was to let the player choose which terrain to [b]keep[/b] or [b]eliminate[/b] at the end of each act.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/22b32f4c6d3405255098a1074cab3348f67fe147.jpg[/img]

When you beat the first boss, [b]The Wall[/b], you must [b]select which terrain you’ll eliminate for good[/b] from the upcoming locations to make room for the [b]Mountains[/b]. The same happens after beating the second boss (which we’ll cover in a future devlog) in order to make room for [b]Wasteland[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/e024fed0e1d20c253107c3c0365704df52589f82.jpg[/img]

Before eliminating a terrain, look at your deck synergies and think about how you gather each resource. If you don’t have any wood-producing cards, don’t forget that eliminating forests will cause you to lose all the wood you’d get from exploration. 
Each option has pros and cons, and that’s part of what makes each run of [i]Drop Duchy[/i] unique.

[h3]Wrap-up[/h3]
Thanks for reading this new devlog! 
Once again, if you have questions or comments, feel free to join the [url=https://discord.com/invite/Ekrchk7fHb]active community on [b]Discord[/b][/url] and come chat with us!

We hope you're ready and as excited as us for [i]Drop Duchy[/i]'s full release on [b]May 5th[/b]! Meanwhile, the demo will remain available if you’d like to play some more runs until then!

In the two remaining devlogs, we'll dive into the [b]third and last Faction called "The Order"[/b], but also into the game’s advanced [b]mechanics[/b], [b]modes[/b] and [b]content[/b] - so [url=https://sleepymillstudio.substack.com/]subscribe to the newsletter[/url] to stay informed!

See you!

notes.title: DEVLOG #3 - Faction Republic & Meta Progression
notes.content:
Hey, everyone!

Welcome to this new devlog!

Since the release of the [b]first demo[/b], lots of you have shared your feedback on the game (thanks!), and some have even started to speculate about the content beyond: How do the other factions play? How can you progress in the game?

Lucky you, I’m here to answer your questions!
In this article, we’ll discuss [b]the second faction[/b] of the game, [b]The Republic[/b], and how the [b]meta-progression[/b] allows you to unlock new powerful strategies.

[b]And if you want to see these in action, you can try out the new demo right now![/b]

[h3]Playing with the The Republic[/h3]
As already discussed in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2525310/view/4451339035198095389]first devlog[/url], the default faction of the game is [i]The Duchy[/i]. 
It’s a simple and well-rounded faction, [b]ideal for beginners[/b] who seek to experiment with [b]varied strategies[/b] and exploit [b]field-based synergies[/b]. 

The second unlockable faction in the game has several [b]exclusive mechanics[/b] that completely renew your strategic options.
First, there is an [b]exclusive terrain[/b] called [b]Neighborhood[/b], which can only be created by cards exclusive to The Republic faction, such as the [b]Downtown[/b]. Neighborhoods, when explored, earn you a new type of resource: [b]citizens[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/33a284258a2c3d4db70e05d5f5463108e08121d2.gif[/img]

When you control this urban faction, your main goal is to create [b]the largest connected neighborhood area[/b] (also known as “the city”) to unleash powerful combos. [b]The Belfry[/b] is the [b]key building of the faction[/b]: you’ll likely use it every round since it has a fantastic potential to generate lots of resources and units when placed adjacent to the city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/3513562af988126a752e2e1ea0e1ab7cd36c5f7d.gif[/img]

The Belfry is also a one-of-a-kind building in the game because you can [b]upgrade it up to level 10[/b], and you get to choose which upgrades to add; would you rather get more military options or increased gold production? Gather bonus units through rivers, fields, or forests? 
With each run, you’ll be able to spend your citizens to upgrade the Belfry differently – discovering all the visual variants and possible combos is a ton of fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/97139ca24d4bb07b4aae7fe3e169d59bbbef82ac.gif[/img]

I must admit that the Republic has been my favorite faction for a while now! It may have to do with its [b]visual style[/b] which was inspired by [b]medieval cities[/b] such as [b]Troyes[/b] and the [b]Republic of Venice[/b]. Who knows…

[h3]Unlocks & upgrades[/h3]
Like any good roguelite, [i]Drop Duchy[/i] has a lot of content to ensure each procedurally-generated run provides enough variety. However, we also learned through playtesting that having access to everything could be overwhelming at first. So, we designed two systems to teach players and add depth over time: [b]faction quests[/b] and [b]challenges[/b].

[b]Faction quests[/b] are exclusive to each faction, and they unlock permanent upgrades for all your future runs such as [b]better starting cards & stats[/b]. The first quests give you an overview of the key mechanics of the faction, while the later ones will genuinely put your skills to the test. Of course, if you want to prove your perfect mastery of a faction, you’ll have to beat the final boss with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/15333120bb6fa9ee8d4cbd700ea5580454f64061.gif[/img]

On the other hand, [b]challenges[/b] can be completed with [b]any faction in any mode[/b] (except tutorial). Objectives range from building a particular deck, using a certain card well, to reaching a specific milestone. 
There’s a challenge for every playstyle, so, make sure to take a look at the list before starting a run; it may give you strategic ideas!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/ee0a3e46fe8ce208ba8de663b87cf35ba54384b6.gif[/img]

Each challenge awards you with “[b]crowns[/b]”, a special currency you keep between runs and can spend in the [b]Progress tree[/b]. 
In this menu, you make your way up to [b]unlock new factions[/b], but also [b]new map locations[/b], [b]mechanics[/b], and [b]card types[/b]. If you like a particular playstyle, you can also unlock more cards in the side branches of the tree to broaden your options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/3538074d984eb78b1f467896978fddf76737ee69.gif[/img]

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
That’s it for today!

We’re really excited to see you experience these new features in this second demo. 
The Republic faction adds a [b]fresh tactical layer to [i]Drop Duchy[/i]’s gameplay[/b], while the meta-progression system ensures that every session feels [b]rewarding[/b] and [b]meaningful[/b]. We’re looking forward to hearing your thoughts on these latest additions!

Stay tuned for our next devlog in which we’ll be revealing more exciting features. 
If you’d like to discuss your experience with the rest of the community, come join us on [b]our official Discord[/b] (we’re already over one hundred there!!): https://discord.com/invite/Ekrchk7fHb

notes.title: DEVLOG #2 - Map, Deckbuilding, and Combat
notes.content:
Hello again!

Thanks for the warm reception on our first devlog, we're delighted to see people intrigued by [i]Drop Duchy[/i]'s [b]unique blend of genres[/b] – how can this be a [b]puzzle[/b], a [b]city builder[/b], a [b]roguelite[/b], and a [b]deckbuilder[/b] all at once, you’ll ask.
Rest assured, you'll understand how each element fits perfectly together after reading this series of articles! 
Or you can… you know… play the demo or watch one of your favorite streamers having a blast.👀

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2525310/announcements/detail/4451339035198095390][b]In the previous devlog[/b][/url], we covered the [b]basics[/b] of placing pieces in the grid to gain resources; today, let’s dive deeper into how you [b]progress[/b] and [b]win a run[/b]!

[h3]Using the map to play your next move[/h3]
A run of [i]Drop Duchy[/i] consists of [b]several rounds[/b]: your goal is [b]to progress as far as possible[/b] despite the increasing enemy presence. If you can [b]reach and defeat the final boss[/b], you win! Each map is procedurally generated: learning to select the right path is essential to optimize your chances of success.

To choose your next location, you must first look at the terrains; each grid provides a different selection of [b]forests, plains, rivers[/b], etc. 
You should focus on [b]picking the one that suits your current deck better[/b], and keep in mind the resources you'll need to upgrade your cards – for instance, forests are ideal for gathering wood in large quantities if that's what you need.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/f5e117e7f25ee1af46cfafa78dc7e98ddadd02f9.gif[/img]

Secondly, you should watch out for [b]hostile regions:[/b] some locations require fighting against enemies, while others don't. Going unprepared for a battle against the enemy could end your run early! 
Choosing a [b]peaceful region[/b] gives you an [b]extra calm round[/b], which may be beneficial to hone your skills, but it also [b]increases the boss' strength[/b] – so, make that decision wisely. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/613f1962f8cb74aea5b80f3f27375379048f77f5.gif[/img]

Finally, you can use the bonus locations available on your way: each [b]guild, depot, trading fair,[/b] etc. grants you additional [b]resources, cards, and buffs.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/ed6a73c275fc80a79bb25bc1f2fbf64b36e141d5.gif[/img]

[h3]Assembling the Perfect Deck[/h3]
In [i]Drop Duchy[/i], you add [b]a new card[/b] to your deck after each round and can collect even more when visiting locations such as the [b]guild[/b] or [b]the university.[/b] 
With each run, you'll be faced with new [b]choices,[/b] and your goal is to assemble a strong and versatile deck based on the available options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/c89cf88e2b8f91075eadaade12d414825ed40a25.gif[/img]

Don’t hesitate to check the [b]deck overview[/b] menu to manage your cards between rounds. You should focus on [b]spending your resources to upgrade their effect,[/b] as their basic form isn't optimal. You can also [b]sell cards[/b] you no longer use and get a refund for all the resources you've spent – it's convenient when you want to pivot your strategy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/29074ad534303da7bfb06b874318ee94d0d2df23.gif[/img]

So, what should you choose in this sea of options? 
Ideally, you would want to find [b]cards that work well together;[/b] in the first devlog, we've shared an example of a [b]combo[/b] based on [b]fields[/b], and we'll tease [b]more synergies[/b] in upcoming articles!

[h3]A Word on Combat[/h3]
Now, let's discuss the [b]combat system[/b], a crucial game component for anyone who wishes to survive long enough (so, basically… everyone). 
Each combat round has two phases: [b]recruitment[/b] and [b]resolution[/b].

At the start of the round, enemy cards get shuffled with your buildings and the location's terrain: [b]the enemy pieces will spawn among the other pieces during the round.[/b]
During this recruitment phase, your goal is to place the enemy pieces in a way that [b]minimizes their recruits[/b] – the less you have to fight, the easier it'll be. Of course, you should also ensure that [b]your military buildings recruit as many units[/b] as possible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/dc473c67d2bb29ad07032e3c279e9b2acb871ed8.gif[/img]

The resolution phase happens at the end of the round once all pieces have been placed. Devise your attack plan by selecting the order in which the groups attack. The outcome is dead simple: just subtract the number of units from both groups.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/bad5ea76973aa24d02bd695e2466ec944e1bccec.gif[/img]

Sounds easy, right? Well, there's a twist to it: each unit type (light, heavy, ranged) has its [b]weaknesses[/b] and [b]advantages[/b] – if you have the advantage over another unit type you will be granted a [b]+50% bonus strength[/b] against them. To optimize your battle outcome, you must be careful about which unit type you’ll send towards the enemy, and use the group merging to your advantage.
Trust me, it can get head-scratching fast: with just 8 groups on the grid, there are already 40000+ different combat orders!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/81a7a062f2fae5a9d6ced7441683790d4d5fd519.gif[/img]

After the combat resolution, you will lose [b]one defense point for each enemy[/b] unit still on the grid. While it might not cause the immediate end of your run, eliminating as many enemies as possible is still a matter of life or death in Drop Duchy.

[h3]Wrap-up[/h3]
That’s it for today! Thanks for reading this new devlog, the whole team hopes you’re having a great time with [b]Drop Duchy’s Demo![/b]

Don’t hesitate to share any questions you may have, I would be happy to answer them!

In the upcoming issues, we'll see about the [b]meta progression, advanced terrains, other factions,[/b] and more, so if you don't want to miss out, subscribe to the [url=https://sleepymillstudio.com/]studio newsletter[/url] to receive updates directly in your inbox.

notes.title: DEVLOG #1 - Resources, farming & tactical combos
notes.content:
Hello, and welcome to the first [i]Drop Duchy[/i] devlog! 

This series of articles will share more information about the game and what’s going on behind the curtain at [i]Sleepy Mill Studio[/i].

First, thank you tremendously for [b]the warm reception[/b] of the announcement. We have reached 10,000 wishlists already, had tons of positive comments, and the trailer got well over 100,000 views on YouTube. For the first game of a new studio, that’s outstanding, so thanks a lot!

We’re working hard on the demo, ironing out the bugs and tweaking the last details. In this upcoming demo, you’ll discover the beginning of the game, strategize around resources, and experience the first faction, [b]The Duchy[/b]. Let’s see what awaits!

[h2]Resources and Exploration[/h2]
Resources are at the heart of the game: you need them to increase the strength of your cards and have a chance of defeating the most dangerous opponents.
The first way to collect resources is called "[b]exploration[/b]," which triggers every time you complete a row.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/98b568823df9232411d5bbec808bf7e6408c9117.gif[/img]

Each natural terrain explored grants [b]resources[/b]: [b]wood[/b] for forests, [b]food[/b] for plains, and [b]gold[/b] for rivers. Buildings don’t give resources when explored, but rest assured they have much more potent effects, as we’ll see in the next part.
To increase your exploration gains, try to play smart: completing several rows simultaneously gives a significant bonus.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/89c0f1fb7b1988c5ac47e7909f0ccfadfd06dd4f.gif[/img]

Exploration is crucial when you don’t have too many cards at the beginning of each run. As you progress, you can enrich your options by selecting cards that improve exploration, such as the technology [b]Optimizer[/b], which increases multi-row bonuses, or the [b]Town[/b], a convenient line-shaped building that's perfectly suited to a super-powerful exploration combo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/f6b2e331a5d3336d1e185ddea3b4829b06430565.gif[/img]

[h2]Fields and The Duchy[/h2]
When you play the demo (and the final game), the first card in your starting deck is the [b]Farm[/b], a building with the power to turn surrounding plains into fields.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/e7b8630bf74d7d9b1bfc1d10e2b8fc9166e98eea.gif[/img]

The starting faction, called [b]The Duchy[/b], are farming specialists, with several exclusive cards themed around fields.
[b]Fields[/b] provide 10 food when explored, a massive upgrade over the 3 food earned when exploring a basic plain. Several cards also benefit from fields, such as the [b]Windmill[/b] (even more food!) or the [b]Watchtower[/b], which recruits three times more units from fields than plains.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/f45a4776e877e0458bac60c93d60ff64ce835569.gif[/img]

Food production shouldn’t be a significant concern when playing The Duchy but don’t forget to collect wood. The best option to do so is the [b]Wood Clearer[/b], a building that turns forests into plains—ideal for creating even more fields!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45096178/483e183dacbe1ef65c0822db0669533b3506aa9f.gif[/img]

Finding and mastering synergies between your cards and the terrain is the key to success in [b][i]Drop Duchy[/i][/b] (and combos are a ton of fun, trust me)!

[h2]Wrap-up[/h2]

That’s it for today; thanks for reading me, and let me know in the comments if you’ve got any questions or topics you’d like to read about in future devlogs.

Next time, I’ll discuss the [b]map[/b], [b]deck-building mechanics[/b], and the [b]combat system[/b]. If you don’t want to miss out, follow us on [url=https://x.com/sleepyMillGames/]Twitter[/url] or subscribe to [url=https://sleepymillstudio.com/]the studio newsletter[/url] to receive updates directly in your inbox.

JB Oger - Game Director
